records.source: וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר־יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And was [the] word of Yahweh to me, saying:
pieces: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me:

L.1: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me, saying:

decisions.choice: chapter 23: the allegory of two sisters, Samaria and Jerusalem, pictured as unfaithful wives
decisions.reason: The chapter tells the history of the northern kingdom (Samaria) and of Judah (Jerusalem) as the story of two sisters whom the LORD married and who were unfaithful to him. Their "lovers" are the great powers Egypt, Assyria and Babylon, whose help and whose gods they sought instead of trusting the LORD. Chapter 16 tells Jerusalem's story in the same way, and Jeremiah 3:6-11 already compared the two sisters. The picture belongs to the prophets' long use of marriage for the covenant between God and his people (Hosea 1-3; Jeremiah 2:2). The language is sexually explicit and the punishments are violent; it is meant to shock the hearers into seeing their betrayal of God.

decisions.choice: Literal follows the Hebrew; Balanced and Readable state the meaning plainly and soberly, adding no detail; the chapter is marked for careful human review
alternatives: softening the language until the meaning is hidden
making it coarser than the Hebrew
decisions.reason: This chapter follows the register rule set for Ezekiel 16 and 23 (see the note at 16:1). Literal keeps the Hebrew's own words and pictures. Balanced and Readable say plainly what is meant, neither blurring it with euphemism nor making it cruder than the Hebrew, and they add nothing that the Hebrew does not say. Where the Hebrew is explicit, the English is explicit in sober words. Every verse of the chapter needs careful review by a named human reviewer before it is approved. The formula "The word of the LORD came to me" keeps the Jeremiah wording.

records.heading: Two sisters, Oholah and Oholibah

records.source: בֶּן־אָדָ֑ם שְׁתַּ֣יִם נָשִׁ֔ים בְּנ֥וֹת אֵם־אַחַ֖ת הָיֽוּ׃
records.gloss: Son of man, two women, daughters of one mother, there were.
pieces: Son of man, there were two women who were daughters of one mother.

L.2: Son of man, there were two women, daughters of one mother.

R.2: Son of man, there were once two women. They were sisters, daughters of the same mother.

decisions.choice: daughters of one mother: one people, Israel, before it split into two kingdoms
decisions.reason: Samaria and Jerusalem were the capitals of the northern kingdom of Israel and of Judah, which came from one people and divided after Solomon's death (1 Kings 12). Jeremiah 3:6-11 also speaks of "faithless Israel" and "her treacherous sister Judah".

decisions.choice: there were once; They were sisters
decisions.reason: Readable marks the start of a story and says that the two were sisters, which "daughters of one mother" means.

records.source: וַתִּזְנֶ֣ינָה בְמִצְרַ֔יִם בִּנְעוּרֵיהֶ֖ן זָנ֑וּ שָׁ֚מָּה מֹעֲכ֣וּ שְׁדֵיהֶ֔ן וְשָׁ֣ם עִשּׂ֔וּ דַּדֵּ֖י בְּתוּלֵיהֶֽן׃
records.gloss: And they prostituted themselves in Egypt; in their youth they prostituted themselves; there were pressed their breasts, and there they handled [the] nipples of their virginity.
pieces: They prostituted themselves in Egypt; even in their youth they prostituted themselves. There their breasts were fondled, and there men caressed them while they were still virgins.

L.3: And they prostituted themselves in Egypt; in their youth they prostituted themselves; there their breasts were pressed, and there [men] handled the nipples of their virginity.

R.3: They were unfaithful in Egypt, like women with many lovers. They did this even when they were young. There men touched their breasts while they were still virgins.

decisions.choice: unfaithful in Egypt in their youth: Israel's idolatry from its beginning, as 20:7-8
decisions.reason: Ezekiel holds that Israel worshiped the gods of Egypt while it was still there (20:7-8; Joshua 24:14). In the picture the sisters were unfaithful from girlhood.

decisions.choice: prostitute oneself: the prophets' picture for worshiping other gods and trusting other powers
decisions.reason: The verb means to act as a prostitute, and the prophets use it for Israel's unfaithfulness to the LORD (Hosea 4:12; Jeremiah 3:1); see the note at 16:1. In this chapter it includes political alliances with Egypt, Assyria and Babylon, which brought the worship of their gods with them.

decisions.choice: their breasts were pressed: the loss of their innocence while young
decisions.reason: The picture is of girls who gave themselves to lovers before marriage. It stresses how early and how willingly the people turned from the LORD.

decisions.choice: plain and sober wording for the sexual picture; the Ezekiel wording for the verb
decisions.reason: The verb follows the wording set for Ezekiel: "prostitute oneself" at Literal and Balanced, and "be unfaithful, like a woman with many lovers" at Readable (see 16:1). The noun follows it: "prostitution" (L, B), "unfaithfulness" (R). Literal keeps "nipples of their virginity"; Balanced and Readable say "while they were still virgins", which is the meaning without added detail.

records.source: וּשְׁמוֹתָ֗ן אָהֳלָ֤ה הַגְּדוֹלָה֙ וְאָהֳלִיבָ֣ה אֲחוֹתָ֔הּ וַתִּֽהְיֶ֣ינָה לִ֔י וַתֵּלַ֖דְנָה בָּנִ֣ים וּבָנ֑וֹת וּשְׁמוֹתָ֕ן שֹׁמְר֣וֹן אָהֳלָ֔ה וִירוּשָׁלִַ֖ם אָהֳלִיבָֽה׃
records.gloss: And their names: Oholah the older, and Oholibah her sister; and they became mine, and they bore sons and daughters. And their names: Samaria [is] Oholah, and Jerusalem Oholibah.
pieces: The older was named Oholah, and her sister Oholibah. They became {{deity_pronoun:mine|Mine}} and bore sons and daughters. As for their names, Oholah is Samaria, and Oholibah is Jerusalem.

L.4: And their names [were] Oholah the older and Oholibah her sister; and they became {{deity_pronoun:mine|Mine}}, and they bore sons and daughters. And their names: Samaria [is] Oholah, and Jerusalem [is] Oholibah.

R.4: The older sister was named Oholah, and the younger was Oholibah. I married them, and they had sons and daughters. Oholah stands for Samaria, and Oholibah stands for Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: Oholah and Oholibah: "her tent" and "my tent is in her"
alternatives: both names meaning simply "tent", with no further point
decisions.reason: Both names come from the word for "tent", which can mean a shrine (the tent of meeting). Oholah means "her tent" and Oholibah "my tent is in her". The names may point to the difference between Samaria, which had shrines of its own making, and Jerusalem, where the LORD's own house stood. They may also recall the tent shrines of idol worship (16:16). The names are kept, and their meaning is given here.

decisions.choice: the older: Samaria, the larger and earlier kingdom
decisions.reason: The northern kingdom was larger than Judah, and its fall came first (verses 9-10). In 16:46 Samaria is also called Jerusalem's "older sister".

decisions.choice: they became mine: God's marriage to his people
decisions.reason: To "become someone's" is to become his wife (Ruth 1:12-13; Ezekiel 16:8). Their sons and daughters are the people of the two kingdoms. That one man should marry two sisters was forbidden by Leviticus 18:18; the picture is not a rule for marriage but a way of speaking about two kingdoms that came from one people.

decisions.choice: I married them; stands for
alternatives: they became mine; Samaria is Oholah
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what "they became mine" means (m3), and that the names stand for the two cities. All levels keep the names Oholah and Oholibah, as set for Ezekiel.

records.source: וַתִּ֥זֶן אָהֳלָ֖ה תַּחְתָּ֑י וַתַּעְגַּב֙ עַֽל־מְאַהֲבֶ֔יהָ אֶל־אַשּׁ֖וּר קְרוֹבִֽים׃
records.gloss: And prostituted herself Oholah while under me, and she lusted after her lovers, after Assyria, warriors,
pieces: While she was still {{deity_pronoun:mine|Mine}}, Oholah prostituted herself. She lusted after her lovers, the Assyrians, warriors

L.5: And Oholah prostituted herself while [she was] {{deity_pronoun:mine|Mine}}, and she lusted after her lovers, after the Assyrians, warriors,

R.5: Oholah was unfaithful to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} while she was still {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wife, like a woman with many lovers. She longed for her lovers, the Assyrians. They were warriors.

decisions.choice: her lovers, the Assyrians: the northern kingdom's dealings with Assyria
decisions.reason: Kings of Israel paid tribute to Assyria and sought its favor: Menahem gave silver to Pul (Tiglath-pileser III) to secure his throne (2 Kings 15:19-20), and Hoshea became Assyria's vassal (2 Kings 17:3). Hosea charges Ephraim with going to Assyria for help (Hosea 5:13; 8:9).

decisions.choice: warriors: an uncertain word
decisions.reason: The word can mean "near ones", and so neighbors or close friends. With the soldiers and horsemen of verse 6, many take it from a related word for battle, "warriors".

decisions.choice: unfaithful to me while she was still my wife, like a woman with many lovers; longed for
alternatives: prostituted herself while mine; lusted after
decisions.reason: The verb follows the wording set for Ezekiel: "prostitute oneself" at Literal and Balanced, and "be unfaithful, like a woman with many lovers" at Readable (see 16:1). The noun follows it: "prostitution" (L, B), "unfaithfulness" (R). "Lusted after" is kept at Literal and Balanced; Readable says "longed for", which keeps the sense of strong desire in plain words. The comma at Literal shows that the sentence runs on into verse 6.

records.source: לְבֻשֵׁ֤י תְכֵ֨לֶת֙ פַּח֣וֹת וּסְגָנִ֔ים בַּח֥וּרֵי חֶ֖מֶד כֻּלָּ֑ם פָּרָשִׁ֕ים רֹכְבֵ֖י סוּסִֽים׃
records.gloss: clothed in blue, governors and commanders, young men of desire all of them, horsemen riding horses.
pieces: clothed in blue, governors and commanders, all of them handsome young men, horsemen mounted on horses.

L.6: clothed in blue, governors and commanders, desirable young men all of them, horsemen riding on horses.

R.6: They wore fine blue uniforms. They were governors and commanders, all of them handsome young men riding on horses.

decisions.choice: blue clothing, governors and commanders: the splendor of Assyria's officials
decisions.reason: Blue or violet dye was costly, worn by the rich and powerful (Jeremiah 10:9). The words for "governor" and "commander" are titles of officials in the Assyrian and Babylonian empires. To the small kingdoms of Israel they looked impressive and attractive.

decisions.choice: desirable young men: the attraction of foreign power
decisions.reason: The picture is of a woman drawn by the looks of her lovers; the reality is a nation drawn by the might of an empire. The same words return in verses 12 and 23.

records.source: וַתִּתֵּ֤ן תַּזְנוּתֶ֨יהָ֙ עֲלֵיהֶ֔ם מִבְחַ֥ר בְּנֵֽי־אַשּׁ֖וּר כֻּלָּ֑ם וּבְכֹ֧ל אֲשֶׁר־עָֽגְבָ֛ה בְּכָל־גִּלּוּלֵיהֶ֖ם נִטְמָֽאָה׃
records.gloss: And she gave her prostitutions to them, the choicest of the sons of Assyria, all of them; and with all whom she lusted after, with all their idols she defiled herself.
pieces: She gave herself as a prostitute to them, to all the elite of Assyria, and she defiled herself with all the idols of everyone she lusted after.

L.7: And she gave her prostitution to them, the choicest of the sons of Assyria, all of them; and with all after whom she lusted, with all their filthy idols, she defiled herself.

R.7: She gave herself to all of them, the best men of Assyria. She made herself unclean with the idols of all the men she longed for.

decisions.choice: with their idols she defiled herself: alliances brought foreign gods
decisions.reason: Political ties with an empire often meant honoring its gods. The northern kingdom's worship of other gods is set out in 2 Kings 17:7-17.

decisions.choice: gave herself as a prostitute (B); gave herself (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew noun; Balanced turns it into a plain verb phrase. Readable says only that she gave herself to them, since the whole verse already says what kind of giving is meant.

records.source: וְאֶת־תַּזְנוּתֶ֤יהָ מִמִּצְרַ֨יִם֙ לֹ֣א עָזָ֔בָה כִּ֤י אוֹתָהּ֙ שָׁכְב֣וּ בִנְעוּרֶ֔יהָ וְהֵ֥מָּה עִשּׂ֖וּ דַּדֵּ֣י בְתוּלֶ֑יהָ וַיִּשְׁפְּכ֥וּ תַזְנוּתָ֖ם עָלֶֽיהָ׃
records.gloss: And her prostitutions from Egypt she did not abandon, for with her they lay in her youth, and they handled [the] breasts of her virginity, and they poured out their lust on her.
pieces: She did not give up the prostitution she had begun in Egypt, for in her youth men lay with her, fondled her breasts while she was still a virgin and poured out their lust on her.

L.8: And her prostitution from Egypt she did not give up, for they lay with her in her youth, and they handled the breasts of her virginity, and they poured out their lust on her.

R.8: She did not stop the unfaithfulness she had begun in Egypt. When she was young, men there had sex with her. They touched her breasts while she was a virgin and satisfied their lust with her.

decisions.choice: her prostitution from Egypt: the northern kingdom's ties with Egypt
decisions.reason: Jeroboam I, who founded the northern kingdom, had lived in Egypt (1 Kings 11:40), and his golden calves recalled the calf made at Sinai (1 Kings 12:28; Exodus 32:4). The last king, Hoshea, sent to Egypt for help against Assyria (2 Kings 17:4; Hosea 7:11).

decisions.choice: plain and sober wording
decisions.reason: "Lay with her" is kept at Literal and Balanced; Readable says "had sex with her", which is plain without being coarse. The rest follows verse 3.

records.source: לָכֵ֥ן נְתַתִּ֖יהָ בְּיַד־מְאַֽהֲבֶ֑יהָ בְּיַד֙ בְּנֵ֣י אַשּׁ֔וּר אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָגְבָ֖ה עֲלֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: Therefore I gave her into [the] hand of her lovers, into [the] hand of [the] sons of Assyria, after whom she lusted.
pieces: So I handed her over to her lovers, the Assyrians she lusted after.

L.9: Therefore I have given her into the hand of her lovers, the hand of the sons of Assyria, after whom she lusted.

R.9: So I handed her over to her lovers, the Assyrians she had longed for.

decisions.choice: handed over to her lovers: the power she courted became her destroyer
decisions.reason: The empire Israel tried to please was the one that destroyed it. God's judgment works through the very thing his people chose instead of him.

records.source: הֵמָּה֮ גִּלּ֣וּ עֶרְוָתָהּ֒ בָּנֶ֤יהָ וּבְנוֹתֶ֨יהָ֙ לָקָ֔חוּ וְאוֹתָ֖הּ בַּחֶ֣רֶב הָרָ֑גוּ וַתְּהִי־שֵׁם֙ לַנָּשִׁ֔ים וּשְׁפוּטִ֖ים עָ֥שׂוּ בָֽהּ׃ס
records.gloss: They uncovered her nakedness; her sons and her daughters they took, and her with the sword they killed; and she became a name among women, and judgments they executed on her.
pieces: They stripped her naked, took away her sons and daughters and killed her with the sword. She became a byword among women, because of the judgments carried out on her.

L.10: They uncovered her nakedness; her sons and her daughters they took, and her they killed with the sword; and she became a byword among women, and they executed judgments on her.

R.10: They stripped her naked. They took away her sons and daughters as captives. They killed her with the sword. Women everywhere talked about her, because of the way she was punished.

decisions.choice: the fall of Samaria: its people killed and carried into exile
decisions.reason: Assyria besieged Samaria for three years and took it in 722 BC; its people were deported to Assyria and other lands (2 Kings 17:5-6; 18:9-11).

decisions.choice: they uncovered her nakedness: public shaming
decisions.reason: A woman punished for adultery could be stripped in public (16:37-39; Hosea 2:5, 12), and captives were led away naked (Isaiah 20:4). The picture joins both.

decisions.choice: a name among women: a byword, an example everyone talks about
decisions.reason: To become a "name" here is to become notorious, an example used as a warning.

decisions.choice: as captives
decisions.reason: Readable says why the children were taken (m1).

records.source: וַתֵּ֨רֶא֙ אֲחוֹתָ֣הּ אָהֳלִיבָ֔ה וַתַּשְׁחֵ֥ת עַגְבָתָ֖הּ מִמֶּ֑נָּה וְאֶת־תַּ֨זְנוּתֶ֔יהָ מִזְּנוּנֵ֖י אֲחוֹתָֽהּ׃

pieces: Her sister Oholibah saw this, yet she was even more depraved in her lust than Oholah, and her prostitution was worse than her sister's.

L.11: And her sister Oholibah saw [it], and she became more corrupt in her lust than she, and in her prostitution [more] than the prostitution of her sister.

R.11: Her sister Oholibah saw all this. But she became even more full of lust than her sister. She was even more unfaithful than her sister had been.

decisions.choice: her sister saw, yet did worse: as Jeremiah 3:7-8 and Ezekiel 16:47-51
decisions.reason: Jeremiah says that Judah saw what happened to faithless Israel and still was not afraid. Ezekiel 16:51 says that Samaria did not commit half of Jerusalem's sins. Judah had a warning before its eyes and did not heed it.

records.heading: Oholibah follows her sister

records.source: אֶל־בְּנֵי֩ אַשּׁ֨וּר עָגָ֜בָה פַּח֨וֹת וּסְגָנִ֤ים קְרֹבִים֙ לְבֻשֵׁ֣י מִכְל֔וֹל פָּרָשִׁ֖ים רֹכְבֵ֣י סוּסִ֑ים בַּח֥וּרֵי חֶ֖מֶד כֻּלָּֽם׃
records.gloss: After [the] sons of Assyria she lusted, governors and commanders, warriors clothed in full splendor, horsemen riding horses, young men of desire all of them.
pieces: She lusted after the Assyrians, governors and commanders, warriors in splendid dress, horsemen mounted on horses, all of them handsome young men.

L.12: After the sons of Assyria she lusted, governors and commanders, warriors clothed in full splendor, horsemen riding on horses, desirable young men all of them.

R.12: She longed for the Assyrians. They were governors and commanders, soldiers in fine uniforms, horsemen riding on horses. All of them were handsome young men.

decisions.choice: Judah and Assyria: King Ahaz's appeal to Tiglath-pileser
decisions.reason: When Judah was attacked by Aram and Israel, King Ahaz sent silver and gold to the king of Assyria, called himself his servant, and copied an altar he saw in Damascus (2 Kings 16:7-18; Isaiah 7).

decisions.choice: clothed in full splendor: in magnificent dress
decisions.reason: The phrase is used again of the army in 38:4. The words of verse 6 are repeated: Judah fell for the same show of power.

records.source: וָאֵ֖רֶא כִּ֣י נִטְמָ֑אָה דֶּ֥רֶךְ אֶחָ֖ד לִשְׁתֵּיהֶֽן׃
records.gloss: And I saw that she was defiled; one way [was] for the two of them.
pieces: I saw that she had defiled herself; both of them went the same way.

L.13: And I saw that she was defiled; [there was] one way for the two of them.

R.13: I saw that she had made herself unclean. Both sisters had done the same thing.

decisions.choice: one way for both: the same conduct
decisions.reason: A "way" is a way of life. Both sisters lived the same way, and so both would come to the same end (verse 31).

records.source: וַתּ֖וֹסֶף אֶל־תַּזְנוּתֶ֑יהָ וַתֵּ֗רֶא אַנְשֵׁי֙ מְחֻקֶּ֣ה עַל־הַקִּ֔יר צַלְמֵ֣י כַשְׂדִּ֔ים חֲקֻקִ֖ים בַּשָּׁשַֽׁר׃
records.gloss: And she added to her prostitutions; and she saw men carved on the wall, images of Chaldeans carved in vermilion,
pieces: But she carried her prostitution further. She saw men pictured on a wall, figures of Chaldeans drawn in red,

L.14: And she increased her prostitution; she saw men carved on the wall, images of the Chaldeans engraved in vermilion,

R.14: But she became even more unfaithful. She saw pictures of men on a wall, pictures of Babylonians painted in bright red.

decisions.choice: men carved on the wall in vermilion: pictures of Babylonian officers
decisions.reason: Babylonian and Assyrian palaces were decorated with carved and painted reliefs of kings and soldiers. Vermilion, a bright red paint, was used for decoration (Jeremiah 22:14). Seeing such pictures, or hearing of Babylon's glory, Judah was drawn to it.

decisions.choice: Babylonians
decisions.reason: The Chaldeans are "Babylonians" at Readable, as set for the prophets. The comma at Literal and Balanced shows that the sentence runs on into verse 15.

records.source: חֲגוֹרֵ֨י אֵז֜וֹר בְּמָתְנֵיהֶ֗ם סְרוּחֵ֤י טְבוּלִים֙ בְּרָ֣אשֵׁיהֶ֔ם מַרְאֵ֥ה שָׁלִשִׁ֖ים כֻּלָּ֑ם דְּמ֤וּת בְּנֵֽי־בָבֶל֙ כַּשְׂדִּ֔ים אֶ֖רֶץ מוֹלַדְתָּֽם׃
records.gloss: girded with belts on their waists, with flowing turbans on their heads, [the] appearance of officers all of them, [the] likeness of [the] sons of Babylon, Chaldea [being the] land of their birth.
pieces: with belts around their waists and flowing turbans on their heads, all of them looking like officers, like the Babylonians whose native land is Chaldea.

L.15: girded with belts around their waists, with turbans hanging down on their heads, all of them with the appearance of officers, the likeness of the sons of Babylon, whose native land [is] Chaldea.

R.15: They had belts around their waists and long turbans on their heads. All of them looked like army officers from Babylon, the land of the Babylonians.

decisions.choice: officers: high-ranking soldiers
alternatives: the third man in a chariot
decisions.reason: The word comes from the number "three" and may first have meant the third man in a war chariot. It came to mean a senior officer (2 Kings 7:2; 9:25).

decisions.choice: flowing turbans: hanging headdresses
decisions.reason: The word describes a headdress with hanging folds or loose ends. The exact style is not certain.

records.source: וַתַּעְגְּבָ֥ה עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם לְמַרְאֵ֣ה עֵינֶ֑יהָ וַתִּשְׁלַ֧ח מַלְאָכִ֛ים אֲלֵיהֶ֖ם כַּשְׂדִּֽימָה׃
records.gloss: And she lusted after them at [the] sight of her eyes, and she sent messengers to them to Chaldea.
pieces: The moment her eyes fell on them, she lusted after them, and she sent messengers to them in Chaldea.

L.16: And she lusted after them at the sight of her eyes, and she sent messengers to them in Chaldea.

R.16: As soon as she saw them, she longed for them. She sent messengers to them in Babylonia.

decisions.choice: she sent messengers to Chaldea: Judah's dealings with Babylon
decisions.reason: Hezekiah welcomed envoys from Babylon and showed them his treasures (2 Kings 20:12-19). Later Judah's kings became Babylon's vassals: Jehoiakim served Nebuchadnezzar for three years (2 Kings 24:1), and Zedekiah was put on the throne by him (2 Kings 24:17).

decisions.choice: paramours: male lovers
decisions.reason: The word is the one usually used for a concubine, a secondary wife. Here it is used of the woman's male lovers, the Egyptians. The use is unusual, and its exact sense is not certain.

decisions.choice: flesh and emission like donkeys and horses: the Egyptians pictured as animals in their lust
decisions.reason: "Flesh" here means the male organ, as in Leviticus 15:2-3, and "emission" the flow of semen. The comparison is deliberately coarse. It shows how base Judah's desire for Egypt's power was, and the prophet's disgust at it. Jeremiah 5:8 uses horses in a similar way.

decisions.choice: Literal keeps "flesh" and "emission"; Balanced says "genitals" and "emission"; Readable says "sexual organs" and "semen"
alternatives: a euphemism such as "who were strong as horses"
decisions.reason: The register rule requires that the meaning be stated plainly without coarse words or added detail. Literal keeps the Hebrew's words, which the reader of Leviticus 15 will recognize. Balanced and Readable use the plain, sober names. This verse needs careful human review.

decisions.choice: Pekod, Shoa and Koa: peoples of the Babylonian empire
decisions.reason: Pekod is known from Babylonian and Assyrian records as an Aramean tribe in eastern Babylonia (compare Jeremiah 50:21). Shoa and Koa are usually taken as peoples east of the Tigris known from the same records. The names also sound like Hebrew words for "punish" and "cry for help", and the prophet may be playing on them.

decisions.choice: the Assyrians with them: soldiers from the former Assyrian lands now under Babylon
decisions.reason: Assyria had fallen to Babylon by 609 BC. The "sons of Assyria" here are most likely troops from its former lands in Nebuchadnezzar's army, or the name is used for all the peoples of Mesopotamia.

decisions.choice: men of renown: men summoned, or famous men
decisions.reason: The word means "called" and can mean those who are summoned to council or those who are well known (Numbers 1:16).

decisions.choice: the peoples of Babylonia
decisions.reason: The Chaldeans are "Babylonians" at Readable; since "Babylonians" comes first in the list, Readable says "the peoples of Babylonia" for the second name.

decisions.choice: my jealousy: God's anger at the betrayal of an exclusive covenant
decisions.reason: God's jealousy is his rightful claim to his people's sole loyalty, like a husband's claim on a wife (Exodus 20:5; 34:14). Ezekiel uses the word for the same picture in 16:38 and 42.

decisions.choice: cutting off the nose and ears: a known punishment in the ancient Near East
decisions.reason: Laws and records from Assyria and Egypt mention cutting off the nose or ears as a punishment, including for adultery, and as a treatment of captives. Here it is part of the picture of a city mutilated and shamed by its conquerors.

decisions.choice: your remnant: those who survive, and what is left of the city
decisions.reason: The word means "what comes after" or "what remains". It refers first to the people who survive and then to everything that is left, which will be burned (2 Kings 25:9).

decisions.choice: cup of punishment
decisions.reason: Readable says what the cup stands for (m1).

records.source: כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהֹוִ֔ה כּ֤וֹס אֲחוֹתֵךְ֙ תִּשְׁתִּ֔י הָעֲמֻקָּ֖ה וְהָרְחָבָ֑ה תִּהְיֶ֥ה לִצְחֹ֛ק וּלְלַ֖עַג מִרְבָּ֥ה לְהָכִֽיל׃
records.gloss: Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: [The] cup of your sister you will drink, the deep and the wide; it will be for laughter and for derision, holding much.
pieces: The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: Your sister's cup you will drink, deep and wide. It will bring you scorn and mockery, for it holds so much.

L.32: Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: The cup of your sister you will drink, deep and wide; it will be for laughter and for scorn, so much it holds.

R.32: This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: You will drink from your sister's cup, a large and deep cup that holds a lot. People will laugh at you and make fun of you.

decisions.choice: it will be for laughter and scorn: Jerusalem will become an object of mockery
alternatives: "you will be laughed at and scorned" (taking the verb as "you will be")
decisions.reason: The verb can be read "it will be" or "you will be". Either way the sense is the same: the cup brings disgrace. Many think the phrase about laughter breaks the description of the cup and may be out of place; the text is followed as it stands.

decisions.choice: the cup of your sister: Samaria's fate
decisions.reason: Jerusalem will suffer what Samaria suffered (verses 9-10). Verses 32-34 have the short lines and repeated sounds of a poem.

records.heading: The cup of her sister

records.source: שִׁכָּר֥וֹן וְיָג֖וֹן תִּמָּלֵ֑אִי כּ֚וֹס שַׁמָּ֣ה וּשְׁמָמָ֔ה כּ֖וֹס אֲחוֹתֵ֥ךְ שֹׁמְרֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: With drunkenness and grief you will be filled, a cup of horror and desolation, [the] cup of your sister Samaria.
pieces: You will be filled with drunkenness and sorrow. It is a cup of horror and ruin, the cup of your sister Samaria.

L.33: With drunkenness and sorrow you will be filled; a cup of horror and desolation [is] the cup of your sister Samaria.

R.33: You will become drunk and full of sorrow. Your sister Samaria's cup is a cup of terror and ruin.

decisions.choice: horror and desolation: a play on two similar words
decisions.reason: The Hebrew words for "horror" and "desolation" sound alike. Together they mean a ruin so complete that it appalls everyone who sees it (5:15; Jeremiah 25:11).

records.source: וְשָׁתִ֨ית אוֹתָ֜הּ וּמָצִ֗ית וְאֶת־חֲרָשֶׂ֛יהָ תְּגָרֵ֖מִי וְשָׁדַ֣יִךְ תְּנַתֵּ֑קִי כִּ֚י אֲנִ֣י דִבַּ֔רְתִּי נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃ס
records.gloss: And you will drink it and drain [it], and its fragments you will gnaw, and your breasts you will tear; for I have spoken, declares [the] Lord Yahweh.
pieces: You will drink it and drain it dry; you will chew on its broken pieces and tear at your breasts. For I have spoken, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

L.34: And you will drink it and drain [it], and its fragments you will gnaw, and your breasts you will tear; for I have spoken, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

R.34: You will drink it all. Then you will chew on the broken pieces of the cup and tear at your own breasts. I have spoken, says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: gnawing the fragments, tearing the breasts: wild grief and despair
decisions.reason: The picture is of someone driven to madness by what she has drunk: she gnaws the broken cup and tears at her own body. The breasts that were handled by her lovers (verses 3, 21) are now torn in grief. The verb "gnaw" is rare, and the exact sense is not certain.

records.source: לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה יַ֚עַן שָׁכַ֣חַתְּ אוֹתִ֔י וַתַּשְׁלִ֥יכִי אוֹתִ֖י אַחֲרֵ֣י גַוֵּ֑ךְ וְגַם־אַ֛תְּ שְׂאִ֥י זִמָּתֵ֖ךְ וְאֶת־תַּזְנוּתָֽיִךְ׃ס
records.gloss: Therefore thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: Because you have forgotten me and cast me behind your back, also you, bear your lewdness and your prostitutions.
pieces: Therefore the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: Because you have forgotten {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and thrown {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} behind your back, you must bear the punishment for your lewdness and your prostitution.

L.35: Therefore thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: Because you have forgotten {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and cast {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} behind your back, you also must bear your lewdness and your prostitution.

R.35: So this is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: You have forgotten {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and turned your back on {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. So you must suffer the punishment for your shameful ways and your unfaithfulness.

decisions.choice: cast me behind your back: rejected me with contempt
decisions.reason: The same words are used of Jeroboam in 1 Kings 14:9 and of the people in Nehemiah 9:26.

decisions.choice: bear your lewdness: bear its punishment
decisions.reason: To "bear" a sin is to suffer its consequences (16:58; 44:10, 12).

decisions.choice: the punishment for
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "bear" means here (m2).

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֵלַ֔י בֶּן־אָדָ֕ם הֲתִשְׁפּ֥וֹט אֶֽת־אָהֳלָ֖ה וְאֶת־אָהֳלִיבָ֑ה וְהַגֵּ֣ד לָהֶ֔ן אֵ֖ת תוֹעֲבוֹתֵיהֶֽן׃
records.gloss: And said Yahweh to me, Son of man, will you judge Oholah and Oholibah? Then declare to them their abominations.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to me: Son of man, will you judge Oholah and Oholibah? If so, confront them with their detestable practices.

L.36: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, Son of man, will you judge Oholah and Oholibah? Declare to them, then, their abominations.

R.36: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, Son of man, are you ready to judge Oholah and Oholibah? Then tell them about the disgusting things they have done.

decisions.choice: will you judge?: a call to bring the charge, as in 20:4 and 22:2
decisions.reason: A second message begins. It sets out the sisters' crimes in the plain terms of the law (verses 37-39) and then returns to the picture (verses 40-49).

decisions.choice: the LORD's words take no quotation marks
decisions.reason: As elsewhere in the book, the LORD's own speech takes no quotation marks, even after "the LORD said to me".

records.heading: Judgment on both sisters

records.source: כִּ֣י נִאֵ֗פוּ וְדָם֙ בִּֽידֵיהֶ֔ן וְאֶת־גִּלּֽוּלֵיהֶ֖ן נִאֵ֑פוּ וְגַ֤ם אֶת־בְּנֵיהֶן֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יָֽלְדוּ־לִ֔י הֶעֱבִ֥ירוּ לָהֶ֖ם לְאָכְלָֽה׃
records.gloss: For they have committed adultery, and blood [is] on their hands; and with their idols they have committed adultery; and even their sons whom they bore to me they have made pass over to them for food.
pieces: For they have committed adultery, and there is blood on their hands. They have committed adultery with their idols, and they have even offered up to them as food the {{gender:children|sons}} they bore to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

L.37: For they have committed adultery, and blood [is] on their hands; and with their filthy idols they have committed adultery; and even their {{gender:children|sons}} whom they bore to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} they have made pass over to them, to be devoured.

R.37: They have committed adultery, and they are guilty of murder. They have committed adultery with their idols. They have even sacrificed to their idols the {{gender:children|sons}} they bore to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, as food for the idols.

decisions.choice: adultery with their idols: idolatry as unfaithfulness in marriage
decisions.reason: Here the picture and its meaning are joined: the "adultery" is the worship of idols.

decisions.choice: made their children pass over to them as food: child sacrifice to idols
decisions.reason: The same charge is made in 16:20-21 and 20:26, 31: children born to the LORD's people were given to idols in the fire. The phrase "as food" says that the idols were treated as devouring them.

decisions.choice: {{gender:children|sons}}
decisions.reason: Child sacrifice took daughters as well as sons (16:20; Jeremiah 7:31), so the inclusive word is used, with "sons" as the alternative.

records.source: ע֥וֹד זֹ֖את עָ֣שׂוּ לִ֑י טִמְּא֤וּ אֶת־מִקְדָּשִׁי֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא וְאֶת־שַׁבְּתוֹתַ֖י חִלֵּֽלוּ׃
records.gloss: Moreover this they have done to me: they have defiled my sanctuary on the same day, and my sabbaths they have profaned.
pieces: They have also done this to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}: on that same day they defiled {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sanctuary and dishonored {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Sabbaths.

L.38: Moreover, this too they have done to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}: they have defiled {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sanctuary on that same day, and they have profaned {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Sabbaths.

R.38: They have also done this to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. On the same day they sacrificed their children, they made {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} temple unclean. They also treated {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Sabbath days with no respect.

decisions.choice: on that same day: the day of the child sacrifices (verse 39)
decisions.reason: The next verse explains: they came straight from killing their children to the LORD's house.

decisions.choice: On the same day they sacrificed their children
decisions.reason: Readable says which day is meant, from verse 39 (m1).

records.source: וּֽבְשַׁחֲטָ֤ם אֶת־בְּנֵיהֶם֙ לְגִלּ֣וּלֵיהֶ֔ם וַיָּבֹ֧אוּ אֶל־מִקְדָּשִׁ֛י בַּיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא לְחַלְּל֑וֹ וְהִנֵּה־כֹ֥ה עָשׂ֖וּ בְּת֥וֹךְ בֵּיתִֽי׃
records.gloss: And when they slaughtered their sons to their idols, they came into my sanctuary on the same day to profane it; and behold, thus they did in [the] midst of my house.
pieces: After they had slaughtered their {{gender:children|sons}} for their idols, they came into {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sanctuary that same day and profaned it. That is what they did inside {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} house!

L.39: And when they had slaughtered their {{gender:children|sons}} to their filthy idols, they came into {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sanctuary on that same day to profane it; and see, this is what they did in the midst of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} house.

R.39: They killed their {{gender:children|sons}} as sacrifices to their idols. Then on that same day they came into {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} temple and treated it as if it were not holy. That is what they did inside {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} house!

decisions.choice: from the idol's altar to the LORD's house: worship mixed with murder
decisions.reason: Jeremiah 7:9-11 makes the same charge: people steal, murder and serve Baal, and then come and stand before God in the temple and say, "We are safe".

records.source: וְאַ֗ף כִּ֤י תִשְׁלַ֨חְנָה֙ לַֽאֲנָשִׁ֔ים בָּאִ֖ים מִמֶּרְחָ֑ק אֲשֶׁ֨ר מַלְאָ֜ךְ שָׁל֤וּחַ אֲלֵיהֶם֙ וְהִנֵּה־בָ֔אוּ לַאֲשֶׁ֥ר רָחַ֛צְתְּ כָּחַ֥לְתְּ עֵינַ֖יִךְ וְעָ֥דִית עֶֽדִי׃
records.gloss: And moreover they sent for men coming from afar, to whom a messenger was sent, and behold, they came; for whom you bathed, painted your eyes, and adorned yourself with ornaments.
pieces: They even sent for men to come from far away; a messenger was sent to them, and they came. For them you bathed, painted your eyes and put on your jewelry.

L.40: And moreover, they sent for men to come from far away, to whom a messenger was sent, and see, they came; for whom you bathed, painted your eyes and adorned yourself with ornaments.

R.40: They even sent messengers to bring men from far away, and the men came. You bathed for them, put on eye makeup and wore your jewelry.

decisions.choice: men from far away, sent for by messenger: envoys from foreign powers
decisions.reason: Behind the picture are Judah's embassies to distant nations seeking alliances (verse 16; Isaiah 57:9).

decisions.choice: bathing, painting the eyes, putting on jewelry: a woman preparing for her lovers
decisions.reason: Eye paint was worn to look attractive, as Jezebel did (2 Kings 9:30); Jeremiah 4:30 uses the same picture of Jerusalem dressing up for lovers who despise her.

decisions.choice: you bathed: the address changes from "they" to "you"
decisions.reason: The verse moves from the two sisters ("they sent") to one woman addressed directly ("you bathed"). Such shifts are frequent in this part of the chapter, and the picture is of the two cities as one.

records.source: וְיָשַׁבְתְּ֙ עַל־מִטָּ֣ה כְבוּדָּ֔ה וְשֻׁלְחָ֥ן עָר֖וּךְ לְפָנֶ֑יהָ וּקְטָרְתִּ֥י וְשַׁמְנִ֖י שַׂ֥מְתְּ עָלֶֽיהָ׃
records.gloss: And you sat on a glorious couch, and a table arranged before it, and my incense and my oil you set on it.
pieces: You sat on a splendid couch with a table laid out in front of it, where you had placed {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} incense and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} oil.

L.41: And you sat on a splendid couch, with a table spread before it, and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} incense and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} oil you set on it.

R.41: You sat on a fine couch with a table set in front of it. On the table you put the incense and olive oil that belonged to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

decisions.choice: a splendid couch and a table spread: a banquet
decisions.reason: Guests at a feast reclined on couches beside a table (Amos 6:4). The woman hosts a banquet for her lovers.

decisions.choice: my incense and my oil: gifts that belonged to God, used for others
decisions.reason: The incense and oil were meant for the LORD's worship, and were his gifts in the first place (16:18-19; Hosea 2:10). Using them for idols or for foreign guests was a further betrayal.

records.source: וְק֣וֹל הָמוֹן֮ שָׁלֵ֣ו בָהּ֒ וְאֶל־אֲנָשִׁים֙ מֵרֹ֣ב אָדָ֔ם מוּבָאִ֥ים סָבָאִ֖ים מִמִּדְבָּ֑ר וַֽיִּתְּנ֤וּ צְמִידִים֙ אֶל־יְדֵיהֶ֔ן וַעֲטֶ֥רֶת תִּפְאֶ֖רֶת עַל־רָאשֵׁיהֶֽן׃
records.gloss: And [the] sound of a crowd at ease [was] with her, and with men from [the] multitude of mankind were brought drunkards from [the] wilderness; and they put bracelets on their hands and crowns of beauty on their heads.
pieces: The noise of a carefree crowd was around her. Along with men from the common people, drunkards were brought in from the desert, and they put bracelets on the women's arms and beautiful crowns on their heads.

L.42: And the sound of a carefree crowd [was] with her; and with men from the common people, drunkards were brought from the wilderness; and they placed bracelets on their hands and crowns of beauty on their heads.

R.42: The noise of a crowd having a good time was all around her. Ordinary men were there, and drunkards brought in from the desert. They put bracelets on the sisters' arms and beautiful crowns on their heads.

decisions.choice: drunkards from the wilderness: the written Hebrew text
alternatives: "Sabeans from the wilderness" (the Hebrew text as traditionally read aloud), meaning traders from Sheba in Arabia
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text is written with a word for "drunkards", but the margin of the Hebrew manuscripts tells readers to read "Sabeans", people of Sheba, who traded across the Arabian desert. The two words differ in one letter. The verse is hard, and either reading fits a rowdy crowd of all kinds of men.

decisions.choice: their hands, their heads: the two sisters
alternatives: the men's own hands and heads
decisions.reason: The men put bracelets and crowns on the women, as gifts to the prostitutes. The pronoun could refer to the men, but the gifts fit the picture of lovers paying the women.

decisions.choice: the women's arms (B); the sisters' arms (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say whose arms are meant (m2).

records.source: וָאֹמַ֕ר לַבָּלָ֖ה נִֽאוּפִ֑ים עַתָּ֛ה יִזְנ֥וּ תַזְנוּתֶ֖הָ וָהִֽיא׃
records.gloss: And I said of [her who was] worn out [with] adulteries, Now they will commit her prostitution, even she.
pieces: Then I said of the woman worn out by adulteries, "Even now men will commit prostitution with her!"

L.43: And I said of [the one] worn out [with] adulteries, "Now they will commit prostitution with her, even with her!"

R.43: Then I said about this woman, who was worn out by her adulteries, "Even now men will still use her as a prostitute!"

decisions.choice: the woman worn out by adulteries is still sought by lovers: the Hebrew is very obscure
alternatives: "Will she now still play the prostitute?" (a question)
"Now she will carry on her prostitution" (reading the verb differently, as the text's margin does)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew of this verse is broken and hard to construe; the written text and the reading in the margin differ in the verb. The drafted sense is that the LORD marvels that men still come to a woman worn out by her many adulteries. No reading is certain.

decisions.choice: the LORD's earlier words in double quotes
decisions.reason: These are words the LORD once said, quoted inside his speech, so they take double quotes.

records.source: וַיָּב֣וֹא אֵלֶ֔יהָ כְּב֖וֹא אֶל־אִשָּׁ֣ה זוֹנָ֑ה כֵּ֣ן בָּ֗אוּ אֶֽל־אָֽהֳלָה֙ וְאֶל־אָ֣הֳלִיבָ֔ה אִשֹּׁ֖ת הַזִּמָּֽה׃
records.gloss: And they went in to her as [one] goes in to a woman, a prostitute; so they went in to Oholah and to Oholibah, the women of lewdness.
pieces: Men went to bed with her as they would with a prostitute; in the same way they went to Oholah and Oholibah, those lewd women.

L.44: And they went in to her as [one] goes in to a prostitute; thus they went in to Oholah and to Oholibah, women of lewdness.

R.44: Men had sex with her as they would with a prostitute. That is how they treated Oholah and Oholibah, those shameful women.

decisions.choice: went in to her: had sexual relations with her
decisions.reason: "Go in to" a woman is the usual Hebrew way of saying to have relations with her (Genesis 16:2; 29:23).

decisions.choice: went in to (L); went to bed with (B); had sex with (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew idiom. Balanced and Readable state the meaning plainly, in the register set for the chapter.

records.source: וַאֲנָשִׁ֣ים צַדִּיקִ֗ם הֵ֚מָּה יִשְׁפְּט֣וּ אֽוֹתְהֶ֔ם מִשְׁפַּט֙ נֹֽאֲפ֔וֹת וּמִשְׁפַּ֖ט שֹׁפְכ֣וֹת דָּ֑ם כִּ֤י נֹֽאֲפֹת֙ הֵ֔נָּה וְדָ֖ם בִּֽידֵיהֶֽן׃ס
records.gloss: But righteous men, they will judge them [with the] judgment of adulteresses and [the] judgment of [women who] shed blood, because adulteresses they [are], and blood [is] on their hands.
pieces: But righteous men will sentence them as adulteresses and as women who shed blood are sentenced, because they are adulteresses and there is blood on their hands.

L.45: But righteous men, they will judge them [with] the sentence of adulteresses and the sentence of [women who] shed blood; for adulteresses they [are], and blood [is] on their hands.

R.45: But men who do what is right will sentence them to the punishment that women receive for adultery and murder. They have committed adultery, and they have blood on their hands.

decisions.choice: righteous men: those who judge rightly, measured by the law
alternatives: the nations, called righteous by comparison with Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The sentence is just: even the instruments of judgment can be called "righteous" in comparison with the sisters, as 16:51-52 says that Jerusalem made her sisters look righteous. Who the righteous men are is not said.

decisions.choice: the judgment of adulteresses and of those who shed blood
decisions.reason: The law punished adultery (Leviticus 20:10; Deuteronomy 22:22) and murder (Genesis 9:6) with death. The same sentence is passed in 16:38.

records.source: כִּ֛י כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה הַעֲלֵ֤ה עֲלֵיהֶם֙ קָהָ֔ל וְנָתֹ֥ן אֶתְהֶ֖ן לְזַעֲוָ֥ה וְלָבַֽז׃
records.gloss: For thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: Bring up against them an assembly, and give them to terror and to plunder.
pieces: For the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: Bring up a crowd against them, and hand them over to terror and plunder.

L.46: For thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: Bring up an assembly against them, and give them over to terror and to plunder.

R.46: This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: Bring a crowd together against them. Let them be terrified and robbed.

decisions.choice: bring up, give over: commands, or "I will bring up"
decisions.reason: The verbs are a form that can be a command or a statement of what will happen. Either way the LORD is the one who brings the judgment.

decisions.choice: an assembly: a gathered crowd that carries out a sentence
decisions.reason: The word is used for the community gathered for judgment (16:40; Numbers 15:35-36). Here it also suggests the gathered army of the nations.

records.source: וְרָגְמ֨וּ עֲלֵיהֶ֥ן אֶ֨בֶן֙ קָהָ֔ל וּבָרֵ֥א אוֹתְהֶ֖ן בְּחַרְבוֹתָ֑ם בְּנֵיהֶ֤ם וּבְנֽוֹתֵיהֶם֙ יַהֲרֹ֔גוּ וּבָתֵּיהֶ֖ן בָּאֵ֥שׁ יִשְׂרֹֽפוּ׃
records.gloss: And will stone them with stones [the] assembly, and cut them down with their swords; their sons and their daughters they will kill, and their houses with fire they will burn.
pieces: The crowd will stone them and hack them down with their swords; their sons and daughters they will kill, and their houses they will set on fire.

L.47: And the assembly will stone them with stones and cut them down with their swords; their sons and their daughters they will kill, and their houses they will burn with fire.

R.47: The crowd will throw stones at them and kill them with swords. They will kill their sons and daughters and burn their houses with fire.

decisions.choice: stoning: the law's penalty for adultery and idolatry
decisions.reason: The law ordered stoning for adultery (Deuteronomy 22:21-24) and for giving children to Molech (Leviticus 20:2). In the history behind the picture, the city's people were killed and its houses burned by the Babylonians (2 Kings 25:9).

records.source: וְהִשְׁבַּתִּ֥י זִמָּ֖ה מִן־הָאָ֑רֶץ וְנִֽוַּסְּרוּ֙ כָּל־הַנָּשִׁ֔ים וְלֹ֥א תַעֲשֶׂ֖ינָה כְּזִמַּתְכֶֽנָה׃
records.gloss: And I will put an end to lewdness from the land, and will be warned all the women, and will not do according to your lewdness.
pieces: So I will put an end to lewdness in the land, and all women will take warning and not act as lewdly as you did.

L.48: And I will put an end to lewdness in the land, and all the women will take warning and not commit lewdness like yours.

R.48: In this way I will put an end to shameful ways in the land. All women will learn from this, and they will not do the shameful things you have done.

decisions.choice: all the women: within the picture, the other cities and peoples who watch Jerusalem's fall
alternatives: a direct warning to women in Israel
decisions.reason: The "women" belong to the picture, as in 16:41, where Jerusalem is punished "in the sight of many women". The chapter is about the faithlessness of Samaria and Jerusalem toward God and what it brought on them. It is not a rule for how husbands may treat their wives, and it gives no one license to harm a woman.

decisions.choice: I will put an end to lewdness in the land: judgment ends the idolatry
decisions.reason: As in verse 27, the judgment will end the long history of unfaithfulness.

records.source: וְנָתְנ֤וּ זִמַּתְכֶ֨נָה֙ עֲלֵיכֶ֔ן וַחֲטָאֵ֥י גִלּוּלֵיכֶ֖ן תִּשֶּׂ֑אינָה וִידַעְתֶּ֕ם כִּ֥י אֲנִ֖י אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃פ
records.gloss: And they will put your lewdness upon you, and [the] sins of your idols you will bear; and you will know that I [am the] Lord Yahweh.
pieces: Your lewdness will be repaid on you, and you will bear the penalty for your sins with idols. Then you will know that I am the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

L.49: And they will bring your lewdness back on you, and you will bear the sins of your filthy idols; and you will know that I [am] the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

R.49: You will be punished for your shameful ways and for your sins of worshiping idols. Then you will know that I am the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: you will know that I am the Lord GOD: the refrain, with the fuller name
decisions.reason: The refrain (see 6:7) here has "the Lord GOD", as in 13:9 and 24:24.

decisions.choice: bear the sins of your idols: suffer the punishment for idolatry
decisions.reason: As in verse 35, to "bear" sin is to bear its penalty.

decisions.choice: Your lewdness will be repaid on you
alternatives: they will bring your lewdness back on you
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "they will put" has no named subject; Balanced and Readable put it in the passive.
